comparison: Perfect agreement on C1 and C2. Both evaluations find the sex-specific photoperiod-induced feeding increase in females to be well-supported with clear and convincing evidence. OpenEval notes statistical significance (p=0.02519 for females), while peer reviewers emphasize the clarity and convincing nature of the behavioral data.

Strong agreement on RNA-seq and validation data (C3, C4, C18-C21, C65). Both evaluations support the molecular findings. OpenEval emphasizes the distinction between increased cell number (agrp1) versus per-cell expression (npyb) including C22, while peer review focuses on the upregulation findings without explicitly discussing C22 in this result.

Agreement on anatomical distribution (C6-C9, C68-C69) and lack of co-expression (C11-C13). Both evaluations find ISH data clear and convincing. OpenEval separates co-expression findings into R4, while peer review groups anatomical and co-expression claims together, noting the contrast with mammalian systems.

Partial overlap on co-expression claims (C11-C13). OpenEval focuses specifically on the comparative finding of non-co-expression versus mammals (C10, C76, C87-C88), while peer review groups this with anatomical data. Both find the evidence clear and note the important species difference.

Perfect agreement on food restriction experiments (C14-C16, C71-C72). Both evaluations find the data statistically significant and convincing. OpenEval emphasizes region-specific changes and internal consistency, while peer reviewers note the clear demonstration of agrp increase and npy decrease with food deprivation.

OpenEval explicitly evaluates the overall conclusion that agrp1, npya, and npyb are feeding-related peptides (C17, C82) as well-supported by combined evidence. No corresponding discrete peer review evaluation found, though this conclusion is implicit in peer acceptance of the overall findings.

Perfect agreement on juvenile experiments (C23-C26). Both evaluations support the finding that sexual maturity, not photoperiod per se, is the key factor. OpenEval emphasizes the statistical non-significance and mechanistic insight, while peer reviewers note this addresses their request for complete analysis of reproductive status effects.

Strong agreement on OVX experiments (C29-C31, C33, C75) demonstrating E2 regulation of agrp1. Both find evidence compelling. OpenEval notes marginal significance (p=0.05790) and includes C27-C28 on feeding behavior, while peer review emphasizes the addition of OVX feeding behavior data as specifically requested and accepted.

OpenEval evaluates npyb's lack of E2 regulation (C32) as clearly supported, distinguishing it from agrp1. Peer review result R6 includes C32 but focuses primarily on agrp1 regulation; the differential regulation of npyb is acknowledged but not emphasized separately.

Agreement on esr2a co-expression with agrp1 (C36, C37, C111) providing evidence for direct E2 regulation. Both evaluations find this convincing. OpenEval includes additional context (C34-C35) and notes appropriate caution about indirect effects, while peer reviewers emphasize this as part of compelling mechanistic evidence.

Strong agreement on agrp1 knockout feeding phenotypes (C38-C42, C117-C118). Both evaluations find the knockout data compelling and well-characterized. OpenEval emphasizes loss of LD/SD difference as particularly compelling, while peer reviewers note this exceeds previous findings and addresses requested molecular characterization.

Agreement on reproductive phenotypes in agrp1 knockouts (C43-C47). Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval notes marginal significance for GSI and questions whether effects are direct or secondary to reduced feeding, while peer reviewers group reproductive and feeding phenotypes together as compelling evidence.

Perfect agreement on the integrative model (C120-C123) linking feeding and reproduction. Both evaluations support this interpretation. OpenEval notes it's well-supported but would benefit from additional validation, while peer reviewers note the expanded discussion strengthens the manuscript and provides fundamental new insight.

OpenEval evaluates literature citations and context claims (C5, C48-C54, C60-C63) as accurately representing cited sources. No corresponding discrete peer review evaluation found, though accurate citation is implicit in peer acceptance.

Strong agreement on medaka model rationale (C55-C59, C64). Both evaluations affirm the value of medaka for this study. OpenEval emphasizes the ability to control reproductive status by photoperiod, while peer reviewers explicitly praise the model choice and note medaka's unique position with strict photoperiodic reproduction and genetic tools.

OpenEval evaluates comparative claims across species (C66-C67, C77-C81, C83-C87, C89-C93) as well-supported by citations. No corresponding discrete peer review evaluation found, though comparative context is acknowledged in peer discussions of species differences.

OpenEval evaluates discussion points (C74, C101-C116) comparing medaka and mammalian mechanisms as well-supported and appropriately cautious. No corresponding discrete peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers note the expanded discussion strengthens the manuscript.

OpenEval rates interpretive claims about timescale and broader implications (C94-C100) as UNCERTAIN, noting they are reasonable but somewhat speculative with limited direct evidence. No corresponding discrete peer review evaluation found addressing these specific interpretive claims.

OpenEval evaluates the mechanistic distinction between cell number versus per-cell expression changes (C22, C73) as well-supported. Peer review R2 includes C22 but does not explicitly emphasize this mechanistic distinction, focusing more broadly on the molecular findings.

OpenEval evaluates contextual claims about reproduction and metabolism (C119, C124) as accurately representing established knowledge. No corresponding discrete peer review evaluation found for these specific background claims.
